mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -1% and HOUST < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST fall by more than 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which is associated with lower corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < previous month for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of declining RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp cut in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by at least 0.75 percentage points within a quarter signals an aggressive easing response to economic stress, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by >= 0.75% within a quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive after a FEDFUNDS cut of 0.75% or more within a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decline of at least 2% in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a synchronized labor and output contraction, which increases recession probability and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month by >= 0.4pp AND INDPRO < previous month by >= 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises by at least 0.4pp and INDPRO falls by at least 2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in the Consumer Price Index above 3% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which prompts anticipatory monetary tightening and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during six consecutive months of CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%.
